stories.title: Big reason why that 1 seed counts so much this year
stories.summary:
Not only do you get the rest and home field advantage throughout, but if you look at the most probable seedings…you’re likely to get a team such as the Browns or Steelers in the divisional round.



	 



	Even if the defense didn’t improve a lick from now to January, i’m still taking those odds against Rodgers at the stage of his career he’s at now or whoever the Browns have at that point…so it’s essentially be the better team for one game at home vs KC/JAX/DEN.



	 



	It was maddening all those years watching the Patriots win 2 games and they made it, but hopefully this is Brady’s approach for the next 7-8 years with Allen.  Path of least resistance, sellout in the regular season for the 1 seed, hope you’re not too banged up and win 2 games

Our D last year in the Jags playoff game
stories.summary:
Bye week is getting long, and with all the talk about our defense this year, I thought I'd rewatch the Jags playoff game to compare (I couldn't bear to watch Denver). Some observations:
	 



	DL: Rousseau looked great, similar to this year. Deone looked really good too. Joey Bosa and AJE were TERRIBLE run defenders, losing the edge on almost every play. Jags averaged 8 yards a rush.



	
	LBs: Shaq Thompson was very good, almost always in the right place and making a positive impact. Milano was very slow, but flowed to the right place. I get why he isn't playing anymore, but like an old head nailing jumpers on the pickup basketball court, his instincts were on point, so the result was a lot better than Dorian Williams.



	 



	DBs: Tre White was the defensive star of the game, created two interceptions by blanketing a receiver and then getting a hand on the ball. Benford was great as ever. Bishop and Poyer were alright, but not horribly out of position at least like CJGJ. Taron Johnson, even though I thought he was washed, was far, far better than Alford. 



	 



	The defense lost the lead three times in the fourth quarter. Luckily, our offense came through with two touchdown drives to win the game. All in all, I wouldn't say our D was performing much better than this year. We gave up the fewest pass yards in the league--but I felt that was more due to teams gashing us with long runs left and right. When a team needed to pass, they often could. To my amateur eye, Shaq Thompson and Tre White could make a big positive impact on the defense.



	 



	Finally, one note on offense: Brandin Cooks looked really good. He got open downfield repeatedly, and made the catch on the biggest play of the game. It bugs me that we have Palmer in there instead of him.

stories.title: Week 8, Nevermores v. Bills, PREDICT THE SCORE!
stories.summary:
Welcome back, everyone!  Coming off the bye week, the Bills host the Nevermores at Highmark.  Rumor has it that Lamar Jackson is returning, and that the O-line of the Nevermores has like 5 new starters.  Should be a cakewalk, right @teef?



	 



	I don't think so.  The reshuffled offensive line is the kiss of death for the Bills D-line.  How many times have we heard over the years that the opposing offensive line has injuries, therefore the D-line should feast?  Instead we get a D-line that puts up about as much fight as a feather duster.  I've got a bad feeling about this game.  Nevermores are 4th in the AFC North, one game back, so they really need this one.  It's a nail biter all the way.  I have the Bills winning uncomfortably:



	 



	Nevermores - 28



	Beews - 34



	 



	Previous winners:



	 



	Week 1 - @colin



	Week 2 - @Freddie's Dead, @HappyDays, @Big Turk



	Week 3 - @Robert Paulson



	Week 4 - @RiotAct



	Week 5 - @Sojourner



	Week 6 - @Reks Ryan, @SydneyBillsFan

stories.title: Is Jim Leonhard actually our prized offseason acquisition
stories.summary: Welp, training camp is underway, we are getting our first peek at new rookie players, players returning from injury that limited their contributions last years, Free Agents etc... Is Jim Leonhard actually going to be the one that has the biggest overall impact on this team... more aggressive defense, using personnel better situationally, great teacher, more fun to watch defense instead of the slow death by 1000 passes and runs drives.... or will he struggle because we need personnel change, system continuity, rookie DC needs to learn etc...  I am holding out hope that he will be the guy we talk about at the end of the year that has had the biggest impact...  Who do you feel will be the person acquired in the offseason that we will look back on and say yeah, this guy was the one.
